problems.title: Released uncertainty and fusion differ from the published algorithm
problems.source_location: main pp. 5-6, Eqs. (2), (4), (5); main p. 8 hyperparameters; supplement pp. 3, 5-6
claim: Main Eqs. (\(2\)), (\(4\)) and (\(5\)), with the supplement's stated schedule, specify squared consistency kernels and continuously weighted clean-latent fusion.
analysis: The printed uncertainty uses squared geometric and photometric errors, whereas the active author-released source uses a cubic photometric kernel and dataset-specific fusion/schedules. A scalar error therefore receives a different confidence even with identical inputs. This supports a specification/release discrepancy, not attribution of the published scores to that exact source revision.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Specify the actual confidence kernels, fusion and dataset schedules; published-score attribution remains unverified.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Frame-dependent backward weights must be reversed with their frames
claim: Supplement Algorithm 1 reverses the latent and guidance sequence but reuses the same frame-dependent weights without an explicit backward-coordinate redefinition.
analysis: Supplement Algorithm 1 reverses the latent and guidance sequences before the backward pass, but retains the same frame-indexed \(\gamma_t\). The weights must follow their frames: \(\widetilde x'_0=(\widehat x'_0+R(\gamma_t)\odot R(g))/(1+R(\gamma_t))\), with elementwise division.

For \(\gamma=[9,0,0]\), \(g=[10,20,30]\) and zero denoised predictions, forward fusion gives \([9,0,0]\). The printed backward rule, realigned to forward order, gives \([0,0,27]\); the reversed-weight rule gives \([9,0,0]\). Blending with \(\beta=[1,0.5,0]\) therefore introduces a spurious final-frame value \(27\) under the literal pseudocode. Zero weights are permitted by Eq. (\(5\)).

The author release already reverses the weights: SVD_2pass_prob_uncertain.py, lines 681-687, flips guidance, masks, latent order and lambda_ts; its Post variant does likewise at lines 693-698. This is a printed-algorithm discrepancy, not evidence that the released generator uses misaligned weights.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Reverse frame-dependent weights together with frames, or explicitly redefine them in backward coordinates; the examined implementation already handles the reversal.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Baseline provenance is insufficient to isolate the reported gain
problems.source_location: main Tables 1 and 3, pp. 8-10; supplement §§B.5 and C.4; repository README
claim: Tables 1 and \(3\) report different DL3DV baseline scores while the full-model score is the same. Their causal comparison requires consistent initialization, losses and budgets.
analysis: Table 1's DL3DV nine-view baseline PSNR is \(12.99\), whereas Table 3's baseline is \(16.59\), both against full-model \(19.19\). The implied gains are \(6.20\) and \(2.60\) dB. This is not automatically a contradiction: the latter baseline includes depth regularization, and the supplement describes stereo initialization. Different losses, initialization, subsets or budgets need a row-level mapping. The paper already specifies every-eighth-image holdout for LLFF/DL3DV and DTU views \(25,22,28\) across \(15\) scenes. Shared SfM camera poses do not by themselves prove held-out appearance leakage.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Release matched baseline initialization, losses and budgets for the compared tables.

problems.title: The no-training statement applies only to the video backbone
problems.source_location: abstract p. 1; method heading p. 4; optimization description pp. 7-8; supplement p. 5
claim: The abstract describes no scene-specific training or fine-tuning, while the method performs iterative Gaussian scene optimization.
analysis: The abstract's no-scene-training wording is broader than the pipeline: each scene undergoes Gaussian optimization for \(10000\) iterations per cycle over three cycles, plus alignment/depth optimization. The valid narrower claim is that the pretrained video backbone requires no scene-specific finetuning. This preserves its reuse benefit while distinguishing preparation cost from feed-forward rendering.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Limit the no-finetuning statement to the video backbone and disclose per-scene Gaussian optimization.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: Zero consistency error does not identify true scene depth
problems.source_location: main Eq. (4), Fig. 3, and reconstruction claims in Figs. 5-7
claim: Equation (\(4\)) uses geometric and photometric consistency to select guidance, and the surrounding discussion associates it with reliable geometry.
analysis: Under pure camera rotation about one optical center, pixel correspondence is a depth-independent homography. In a constant-color region, arbitrary positive assigned depth can therefore yield zero geometric cycle error and zero photometric error, so Eq. (\(4\)) gives \(U=0\) despite wrong depth. This is a scoped observability counterexample, not a statement that the benchmark has only degenerate scenes. Reported image-quality improvements and existing geometric/photometric ablations remain evidence of rendering benefit, without proving metrically correct geometry.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Describe consistency as internal agreement rather than calibrated true-depth confidence.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.

problems.title: Reported gains and partial timing do not establish significance or total cost
problems.source_location: main pp. 8-9; checklist pp. 17-18; supplement §C.3, pp. 6-7
claim: The reported comparisons and supplement timing are used to discuss superiority and efficiency.
analysis: The checklist explicitly discloses absent significance reporting. The small \(0.17\) dB LLFF lead lacks a paired scene/run uncertainty analysis; larger observed differences do not remove that uncertainty. Compute information is provided: about \(30\) minutes of Gaussian optimization per cycle and \(20\) minutes for one \(25\)-frame clip on an NVIDIA A40. Three training cycles give roughly \(90\) minutes of that component. With \(p\) clips per generation round and \(k\) rounds, \(90+20pk\) minutes is only serial component arithmetic; it omits initialization, alignment, transfer and any reuse/parallelism.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Report paired scene uncertainty and end-to-end cost with component accounting.

problems.title: Diffusion time units and nonnegative spatial weights need a common definition
problems.source_location: Main PDF: diffusion notation, p. 4; Eqs. (2) and (5), pp. 5-6. Supplement: p. 2 and schedule/Algorithm 1, pp. 5-6.
claim: The main schedule is normalized to the unit interval, the supplement uses a reverse-step scale near \(100\), and a nominally positive scalar weight later becomes spatial and may be zero.
analysis: The main schedule uses a threshold on \([0,1]\), while the supplement uses \(\tau=70\overline U+30\) on a reverse-step scale near \(100\). At \(\overline U=0.5\), these conventions give \(0.65\) and \(65\). State whether the comparison is \(t/T\le0.7\overline U+0.3\) or \(t\le T(0.7\overline U+0.3)\), and distinguish reverse indices from scheduler noise timestamps.

The preliminaries write \(g^2(x)\) although the diffusion coefficient is \(g(t)\), and call \(\sigma_t\) a variance while using \(dx=(x-\widehat x_0)\,d\sigma/\sigma\). With variance \(v=\sigma^2\), the equivalent expression is \(dx=(x-\widehat x_0)\,dv/(2v)\).

Eq. (\(2\)) calls \(\gamma_{t,i}\) a positive scalar, but Eq. (\(5\)) allows zero and spatial variation. Nonnegative diagonal/broadcast weights resolve the type issue. The unweighted quadratic term keeps the Hessian positive definite, so Algorithm 1's elementwise minimizer is correct, including zero-weight entries.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Use one explicit diffusion-time convention and nonnegative broadcast weights; the weighted-quadratic minimizer remains valid.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The pose-selection heuristic has a chosen translation scale
claim: Supplement Eq. (S-8) combines translation distance and angular distance with coefficients set to one.
analysis: The pose score combines translation distance with angle using unit coefficients. Candidate \(A\) with distance \(0.1\), angle \(0.8\) radians scores about \(0.40657\); candidate \(B\) with distance \(0.5\), angle zero scores \(0.60653\). Multiplying translation coordinates by ten gives \(0.16530\) and \(0.00674\), reversing their ranking under a unit change. Normalize scene scale or specify reciprocal-unit coefficients. The author function correctly converts camera centers, so that separate error is not alleged. A pose heuristic need not measure actual occlusion/field-of-view overlap.

Equation (S-8) explicitly introduces two balancing parameters and fixes them for the reported implementation. Its dependence on translation units does not alone refute a stated scale-invariance theorem, because no such theorem is given. A reproducible implementation should keep the same scene scaling and parameter convention; changing units without transforming the coefficient changes the heuristic itself.
result: The constructed ranking reversal establishes unit sensitivity, not a current mathematical error in a fixed-scale pose-selection heuristic. Its correspondence to actual covisibility remains an empirical question.
problems.impact_rationale: No current-error impact: the source specifies a parameterized heuristic, and scale invariance is not an established author claim.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper repair is required merely because the fixed-scale heuristic is not invariant to an unaccompanied change of units.

problems.title: SDS improves some displayed metrics but worsens LPIPS
problems.source_location: Supplement: Table S-1 and discussion, p. 6; main PDF: Table 3.
claim: Supplement Table S-1 and the discussion describe baseline improvement from image inpainting.
analysis: Supplement Table S-1 reports SDS PSNR \(18.12\), SSIM \(0.551\), and LPIPS \(0.738\), compared with RePaint LPIPS \(0.403\) and the full model's 0.335. The \(0.738\) value is visible in the rendered PDF. If Table 3's baseline LPIPS \(0.405\) is the intended comparator, SDS worsens that metric despite improving PSNR and SSIM. The prose that image inpainting improves the baseline should state which metrics and baseline are meant. This does not justify guessing that \(0.738\) is a typo or replacing it with a more convenient number.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: State the metric-specific SDS pattern without guessing a replacement for the displayed LPIPS value.
